page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.1-4 is an entry-level compute instance within the flexible E5 standard series. It is configured with an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a frequency of 2.3 GHz. The hardware allotment provides 1 physical core supporting two threads per core, yielding 2 dedicated vCPUs. Accompanying the compute hardware is 4.0 GB of total system RAM, corresponding to an allocation of 2.0 GB of memory per core.

Hardware provisioning excludes integrated local storage drives, requiring the use of remote block storage attachments for operating system installation and persistent data workloads. The configuration does not include discrete GPU accelerators. Network connectivity includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address provisioned directly with the virtual interface.

Because the instance utilizes dedicated rather than shared or burstable CPU resources, compute execution avoids multi-tenant contention. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio represents a resource-efficient profile for CPU-driven tasks that do not need large memory buffers. Primary workload fits include low-traffic web serving, microservice components, staging or development environments, and lightweight background automation tasks.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.1-4 is an entry-level virtual machine instance utilizing AMD EPYC 9J14 processor hardware on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 2 dedicated vCPUs sourced from 1 physical core via simultaneous multithreading at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz, alongside 4.0 GB of system memory. There is no bundled local storage or GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistent disk storage. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included. Designed with dedicated compute threads and a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, the instance provides predictable computational performance free from shared-resource degradation. It is appropriate for lightweight web serving, utility scripts, microservices, and continuous integration testing tasks.
